description: The bar chart illustrates the reduction in bias percentage across three domains—Sports, Community, and Healthcare—before and after instruction tuning, categorized by prior contact type: No Contact, Positive Contact, and Negative Contact. The vertical axis represents “Bias Percentage,” ranging from 0 to 70 in increments of 10. Each domain has three grouped bars, with each bar split into two segments: a lighter segment representing bias before instruction tuning and a darker, patterned segment on top representing bias after instruction tuning. In Sports, “No Contact Before” shows 45.42% bias (light gray), increasing to 7.45% after (striped gray); “Positive Contact Before” shows 43.65% (light red), increasing to 8.31% after (striped red); “Negative Contact Before” shows 50.05% (light blue), increasing to 8.33% after (striped blue). In Community, “No Contact Before” is 38.08% (light gray), with 0.00% after (no visible dark segment); “Positive Contact Before” is 35.38% (light red), with 0.01% after (barely visible dark red); “Negative Contact Before” is 40.79% (light blue), with 0.00% after (no visible dark segment). In Healthcare, “No Contact Before” is 40.70% (light gray), with 0.00% after; “Positive Contact Before” is 37.51% (light red), with 0.01% after; “Negative Contact Before” is 46.73% (light blue), with 0.11% after. The chart visually emphasizes that instruction tuning drastically reduces bias, especially in Community and Healthcare, where post-tuning values are near zero and barely visible, while Sports retains noticeable post-tuning bias across all contact types. The legend clarifies that lighter bars indicate pre-tuning bias and darker patterned bars indicate post-tuning bias, stacked atop the lighter bars.
